title: Rocks, fossils, and landforms
description: Test what you know about Alberta's fossils, boulders, and oil sands with a three-question quiz.
overviewDescription: Answer three multiple-choice questions about Alberta's badlands, glacial boulders, and oil sands. Each correct answer adds a note to your expedition journal.

activity.introduction: Alberta's landscape holds clues about ancient life and powerful ice. Answer three questions to add each discovery to your journal.

complete.title: Quiz complete!
complete.description: You added three geology discoveries to your expedition journal.

questions.prompt: Which part of Alberta is famous for badlands and dinosaur fossils?

options.correct: The Red Deer River valley near Drumheller

questions.correct: That's right! In 1884, geologist Joseph Burr Tyrrell found a dinosaur skull in the badlands near Drumheller. It was later named Albertosaurus.
questions.tryAgain: Not quite. Think of the dry, layered badlands where fossils are exposed along a river valley. Try another answer!

questions.prompt: How did the huge Big Rock boulder near Okotoks travel from the Rocky Mountains?
questions.correct: That's right! Glacial ice carried Big Rock out of the Rocky Mountains and left it near Okotoks.
questions.tryAgain: Not quite. This boulder is so large that only something enormous and slow-moving could carry it. Try another answer!

questions.prompt: In which part of Alberta are the oil sands mainly found?

options.wrong: Southern Alberta near the U.S. border

questions.correct: That's right! Alberta's oil sands are found in northern Alberta, including the Athabasca, Cold Lake, and Peace River areas.
questions.tryAgain: Not quite. Think of the region around Fort McMurray. Try another answer!
